body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Winnie the Pooh is turning 100, and the Hundred Acre Wood is getting a high-fashion makeover to celebrate.

	Los Angeles-based fashion brand Re/Done has teamed with Disney on a four-piece Winnie the Pooh capsule collection, arriving Sept. 3 as part of the yearlong celebration marking a century since A.A. Milne first introduced the honey-loving bear in 1926’s “Winnie-the-Pooh.”

	The collection puts Pooh and his Hundred Acre Wood crew across the denim label’s signature vintage-inspired silhouettes. The lineup includes the Classic Tee Pooh Friends and 50s Boxy Tee Oh Bother, both priced at $160, alongside the $495 Silly Bear Cardigan and $550 Storybook Crew. Pooh, Piglet, Tigger and Eeyore appear throughout the collection in artwork designed to evoke the characters’ storybook roots.



						
			
	

	
					

	The capsule arrives amid a wide-ranging centennial celebration that Disney has been rolling out throughout 2026.  Random House released “Wonders of the Hundred-Acre Wood Treasury” earlier this week, while “Winnie the Pooh: 100 Mindful Moments,” a new book built around the character’s famously simple approach to life, arrives Sept. 22. Penguin Random House is also hosting anniversary events this fall, including an Oct. 10 celebration at the New York Public Library and programming across dozens of its local branches. 

	For Re/Done, the Pooh drop is the latest installment in a growing relationship between Disney and the brand.  The partnership began last fall with a Mickey & Friends collection inspired by Disney artwork from the 1920s. A second installment followed in February with vintage-style shirts featuring characters from Disney’s Golden Age, including Dumbo, Bambi, Pinocchio and Jiminy Cricket.  Earlier this year, the label also teamed with Disney and 20th Century Studios on a “The Devil Wears Prada 2” capsule timed to the sequel’s theatrical release. All are still available to shop on the Re/Done website.

title: Dark Comedy ‘Down to Die’ Marks Actress Marta Pozzan Directorial Debut (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
Actress and producer Marta Pozzan will make her directorial debut with the dark comedy short “Down to Die.”

	The film follows two friends, Maria (P
body:
Actress and producer Marta Pozzan will make her directorial debut with the dark comedy short “Down to Die.”

	The film follows two friends, Maria (Pozzan) and Gabriel (Andrew Matarazzo), whose seemingly ordinary afternoon at an exclusive members-only club in East Los Angeles East spirals into a candid conversation about aging, ambition, identity and mortality.

	Pozzan directs from her own script.


	Alongside Pozzan (“Fior Di Latte,” “From Scratch”) and Matarazzo (“Teen Wolf”), the cast also includes Joe Apollonio (“Magic Farm”) as Reece, the club’s ever-present membership curator whose interruptions are never quite accidental, and Lindsey Normington (“Anora”) as Noah, the effortlessly charming waitress who briefly cuts through the emotional tension with a grounded warmth.
	

	The project explores themes of performative success, celebrity obsession and emotional detachment through rapid-fire dialogue and uncomfortable comedic tension.

	“Down to Die” is produced alongside Kaley Ronayne, Nuer Taqa and Radiance Pictures, with cinematography by Ksusha Genenfeld, who previously shot “Perfect” with Julia Fox, editing by Sabrina Greco (“Lockjaw”), and casting by Kate Geller (“Shiva Baby”). 

	Pozzan has contributed to a range of independent productions over the past five years, with projects premiering at the Tribeca Film Festival, the Stockholm Film Festival and the Belfast Film Festival, all while collaborating with award-recognized creative teams. She co-produced both “Fior Di Latte” starring Julia Fox, Tim Heidecker, and Kevin Kline alongside the producers of Josh and Benny Safdie’s “Good Time”, as well as “The Dregs” with Emmy nominee Nava Mau.
	

	Pozzan and Apollonio are represented by Untitled Entertainment. Normington is represented by Authentic and Innovative Artists, while Matarazzo is represented by Luber Roklin and Innovative Artists.

	(Pictured above: Pozzan, Matarazzo, Normington and Apollonio)

title: Gloria Steinem’s Farewell Interview to Stream on Netflix
description: Feminist icon Gloria Steinem is the third subject to now appear on Netflix’s “Famous Last Words,” the series that banks interviews with notable figu
body:
Feminist icon Gloria Steinem is the third subject to now appear on Netflix’s “Famous Last Words,” the series that banks interviews with notable figures meant to be shared only after their death. 

	Steinem died Wednesday at her home in New York City. She was 92. Her interview with host and executive producer Brad Falchuk was conducted in February 2025 and recorded in private, per the show’s format, and held until after her passing — as a means to share what she hopes will be seen as her final message to the world.
	

	The first episode of “Final Last Words” featured chimpanzee expert and conservationist Dr. Jane Goodall, who died in October 2025, followed by an episode in February that ran after the death of actor Eric Dane.


	Per Netflix, the interview with Steinem touches on her role “as a lifelong traveler on the road to justice. While the world often recognizes her as a face of modern feminism, this interview delves into her deep-seated interests in the shared origins of sex and race caste systems, the cultures of Indigenous peoples, and the vital necessity of organizing across boundaries for equality. Steinem also takes advantage of the Famous Last Words format to speak freely about her loves, her family, the complicated personal politics within the feminist movement and her regrets.”

	Steinem helped launch Ms. magazine, which was at the forefront of the movement to help organize and promote the voices and concerns of women in society. She also helped establish the Women’s Action Alliance, and wrote books including her 2015 memoir, “My Life on the Road.”
	

	Steinem was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by President Obama in 2013.

	“Gloria Steinem was the steady heartbeat of a revolution, but in this room, she was a woman reflecting on the simple, profound beauty of human connection,” Falchuk said. “She spoke about the intersection of race, gender, and peace with a wisdom that only comes from a lifetime on the front lines. Even in her final moments, she was organizing us, challenging us to keep moving forward. It is an extraordinary privilege to share her final thoughts with the world.”

	Based on the Danish format Det Sidste Ord, “Famous Last Words” is taped in a closed-door recording session. And keeping the privacy of the recording, the chat will be shot by remotely operated cameras. At the end of the interview, subjects (including Steinem) are asked to look into a camera and give their final message, their last words to the world. The footage is then kept confidential until the subject’s passing.

	The series is executive produced by Falchuk and Mikkel Bondesen through the Brad Falchuk Teley-Vision banner, alongside BSNA (a Banijay Entertainment company), David Goldberg and showrunner David Friedman.

	The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts is also an executive producer and the home of the show’s archives. 



	

	



	Meanwhile, although the “Famous Last Words” interview will be the final chat with Steinem that is posted, it actually wasn’t quite her last interview. On Sept. 17, Audible plans to release Steinem’s final public appearance, which took place July 14 and 16 at its Minetta Lane Theatre in New York.Those two evenings, dubbed “Yes to the Unknown: A Night with Gloria Steinem,” were led by Amy Richards, who conducted conversations with Steinem, and also featured Keri Russell, who performed excerpts from Steinem’s writing during the July 14 show.

title: ‘The Gentlemen’ Producers on Balancing Quirkiness With Crime in ‘Glamorous’ Season 2: ‘We Are Always Looking for New Ways To Murder People’
description: If “Bridgerton” gave British stately homes a new lease of life with a sprinkle of Regency charm, “The Gentlemen” has injected them with a criminal d
body:
If “Bridgerton” gave British stately homes a new lease of life with a sprinkle of Regency charm, “The Gentlemen” has injected them with a criminal dose of cool.

	The Guy Ritchie show, which stars Theo James as a Duke gone bad opposite Kaya Scodelario’s gangland heiress Susie Glass, returns to Netflix for its second season today with more guns and more glamor. But it’s the series’ unabashed Britishness – delivered via the afore-mentioned country estates interspersed with panoramic shots of the London skyline – coupled with a slick script and stand-out action sequences that have made the show so popular. (It has already been renewed for Season 3).
	

	“Americans are obsessed with the British, whether we want to admit it or not,” says Jonathan Glickman, CEO of Miramax and an executive producer on the “The Gentlemen.”


	(Leaning into the theme, the Season 2 premiere took place on Wednesday at the medieval Guildhall in London, with actors clad as Vinnie Jones-inspired groundskeepers patrolling both ends of the red carpet with dogs.)

	“The Gentlemen’s” DNA can be traced back to Ritchie’s own appreciation for the country’s culture and history. “He’s his own version of Eddie Horniman,” explains costume designer Loulou Bontempts, who says the director takes a keen interest in the smallest costuming details, even down to fabric. “Tailoring is so important,” she says. “And the history behind British aristocracy and British quintessential country dressing. You know, there really are rules.” 



	

	



	Many such rules – for example, only the lord of the manor is allowed to wear a red velvet jacket at home — are strictly adhered to but unspoken, precisely to trip up outsiders, as newcomer Cico Maldini (played by Michele Morrone) finds out to his cost.
	

	Having introduced audiences to the barmy world of the British aristocracy in Season 1, the show goes international in Season 2, as Eddie and Susie (Scodelario) expand their operations onto the Mafia’s home turf. “Italy felt like a very logical place in terms of the fame of the Mafia, but also the glamor,” says Read, who also executive produces the show. Cue plenty of salivating shots of Italian palazzos basking in the sun.

	Season 2 certainly notches up the glamor, both at home and abroad. Bontempts notes that both Eddie and Susie’s wardrobes have gotten an upgrade now they’re making serious money, with the duke’s suits better cut and Susie sporting a Birkin, while props include classic cars, fine wines and even a tiger. Glickman declined to share details of the budget but credits the producers and crew with “maintain[ing] the scale and scope by smartly deploying resources.” So the suits are pinned in-house, the props are on loan and the tiger is entirely CGI – although its cage was real.

	“I found this this steel gazebo on eBay for £20,000 [$27,000],” laughs production designer Martyn John. “Put sides on it, put bars on it, and that became the tiger’s cage.” However he reveals the budget didn’t extend to shooting the tiger scene on location in Italy so instead he found a suitable garden in the U.K. and peppered it with Italianate sculptures.

	The tiger storyline (too delicious to give away as a spoiler here) is typical of the show’s campy yet cool tone, blending glamor with surrealist violence. “The tone of the show is reality plus 7%,” says Read of the principle he and Ritchie hold on to while writing. Although considering Season 2 also introduces a mythical Slavic figure known as a Bannik, “sometimes I think it’s more like 8%,” Read acknowledges.

	Glickman promises even more action for Season 2 (he says Episode 7 in particular is “wall to wall action”) but not at the expense of character development, as Eddie looks set to double cross Susie while their relationship increasingly oscillates between business and pleasure. “Action works when you have an emotional attachment to the people that are in the action scene,” Glickman points out.

	For Read, striking a balance between action and emotion, violence and humor is something he and Ritchie discuss constantly during the writing process. “We talk about tone a lot, Guy and I, when we’re making the show, and encouraging each other to push ideas to unexpected places, surprising places,” Read explains. “You can’t push it too far because you need to balance that with credibility and emotional stakes.”
	

	“But yes,” he adds, “we are always looking for new ways to murder people.”

schema.headline: ‘The Gentlemen’ Producers on Balancing Quirkiness With Crime in ‘Glamorous’ Season 2: ‘We Are Always Looking for New Ways To Murder People’

title: Jane Fonda on Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger, Trump and Tech Bros’ Desire for Longevity ‘While They’re Killing the Rest of Us’
description: A feisty Jane Fonda on Thursday spoke out about her opposition to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, her aversion to Donald Trump, and the eerie des
body:
A feisty Jane Fonda on Thursday spoke out about her opposition to the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, her aversion to Donald Trump, and the eerie desire that “tech bros, oligarchs and billionaires” have for longevity, “while they’re killing the rest of us,” as she put it.

	Fonda, 88, took questions from a small group of journalists prior to being honored at the DVF Awards charity gala held on the sidelines of the Venice Film Festival by fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg to honor extraordinary women. The event’s other honorees were the Prime Minister of Barbados Mia Amor Mottley; American photojournalist Lynsey Addario; Kenyan social entrepreneur Wawira Njiru and France’s feminist icon Gisèle Pelicot. 
	

	Though the bulk of the conversation with Fonda was about politics, her activism and the tyranny of tech bros, the two-time Oscar winner also provided an update on her career as an actress.


	“The Correspondent,” Lionsgate’s film adaptation of Virginia Evans’ bestselling novel about a retired lawyer who uses letter-writing to impose order on a complicated world, is now in final stages of pre-production, she said. Fonda hopes cameras will start rolling in January, though “it depends on the director.” And she has other projects percolating: “I just can’t mention them.”

	It’s clear that Fonda is eager to get back in front of the camera.

	“After five years of not working as an actor, I have to confess that — as much as I love the work that I do with my comrades in the movement — I miss the process of becoming somebody else. It is such a thrilling process. I love it. I miss it,” she underlined.
	

	You recently defended Mark Ruffalo’s First Amendment right to speak out about politics and powerful corporations in the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, which you are opposed to. What is your main concern regarding the prospect of this merger? 

	I am hopeful that we can stop it. They’re carrying so much debt. The Ellisons are carrying so much debt, and it’s being postponed now, so that they have to pay these huge sums. The merger would be terrible for consumers. Prices would go up. Thousands and thousands of people would lose their jobs. And as a creative, the fewer studios there are, the fewer places that we can take our products. We lose bargaining power. Unions lose their power. There’s a very robust and growing movement to stop the mergers. And it, you know, it’s sad for me because I like David Ellison very much. David’s Skydance financed “Grace and Frankie,” my seven-year-long run for Netflix, and I got to know him, and I like him. But that doesn’t change things. This is not a personal thing. This is what it will do to the entertainment industry, which is already suffering terribly.

	How how do you think Ted Turner would have felt about the prospect of Paramount owning CNN?

	Oh, I think he would be terribly upset. He didn’t want to sell back in the day when he sold, and I was still with him then. And I remember all of the big thinkers, you know, the John Malones, the Gordie Crawfords. They were all saying, “You’ve got to do this.” Ted didn’t want to do it, but he did. And now David Zaslav did. Ted would be absolutely heartbroken.

	You stood up for Mark Ruffalo when he was accused of antisemitism. Do you think there’s a blacklist now in Hollywood?

	Absolutely. I mean, this is a tactic that they’re they’re using. Larry Ellison, because he doesn’t like Mark Ruffalo’s position on the merger, accuses him of antisemitism, when he said nothing that that isn’t within his constitutional right to say. It’s a tactic they’re using. He should be ashamed of himself, Larry Ellison. But there’s a lot of support for Mark. A lot of people came forward.

	You started becoming a political activist very young. How important was it for you to take political positions?

	I was 33 years old when I became an activist. And my life before then was so silly. So nothing. So meaningless. And when I became an activist I met entirely different kinds of people. Back in the 1970s, around Vietnam, there was a backlash. But I was part of a movement. I was not alone. This is very important. Mark is part of a movement. He’s not alone. This is a time when we have to stick together. We can’t be alone. They can’t pick us off when we’re alone. 
	

	Has it become harder to speak out about things since Donald Trump’s rise?

	Not for me. No. I’ve had my life. He can do nothing to me. I’m not scared. But that’s not true for everyone, and I understand that. And that’s why I’m encouraging people to join the movement. I created the committee for the First Amendment a year ago, on Oct. 1. It existed in the 1940s and ’50s as a way to confront McCarthy and the witch hunts. My dad was a member. And we have thousands and thousands of members, and we have them come together. We’re building community.

	What happens to normal people who are not you? How do you see the fact that it’s more difficult for them to speak out?

	More and more of them are speaking out. I’ll tell you why. Their whole lives are at risk right now. AI could take away their jobs. And then data centers are being put into their neighborhoods that are destroying [the environment]. There’s been a shift in the U.S. Things are changing. Republicans and Democrats alike are standing there saying, “No. You’re not going to put a data center in my community.” No, you’re not going to put a detention center.” We can see now that MAGA members, even, they’re not liking the fact that their leaders are profiting off misery and cruelty. They don’t like that. They don’t like the chaos that’s happening. They don’t like the way the immigrants are being treated.

	Do you have a presidential candidate that you like for 2028?

	You know, it’s too soon. We don’t know what’s going to happen. I can tell you though. I’m looking at Jon Ossoff. Aside from the presidential race aside, there are some young politicians I like. Justin Pearson [the Tennessee State Representative who is running for Congress in November], for example. There’s a woman, Peggy Flanagan, [Lieutenant Governor of Minnesota since 2019 who is a Democrat running for the United States Senate in 2026]. She’s an Indigenous woman, Ojibwe from Minnesota. She’s going to get into the Senate. I mean, imagine if we had senators who thought, “Hmm, the decision I’m going to make now. How is it going to affect people seven generations from now?”

	Within the global elites, longevity seems to be all the rage. What are your thoughts on that?

	They want to live forever, while they’re killing the rest of us. There’s two things: Most of these guys, these tech bros and these oligarchs and billionaires, they feel that the laws that the rest of us live by don’t matter to them, including the laws of physics. Natural laws. They’re going to live forever. That’s one [thing]. The other is that because these [ageless] guys can’t have babies, they’ll create robots. That’ll be their babies. And they’ll just turn the rest of us into tradwives, who have a lot of babies too. Then they’ll take away the vote. Can you believe it? And we’re not going to stand for it. They’re not going to win, because we’re not going to stand for it. The big problem is — and this has never happened in the history of humankind — if this was happening at any other time, you could say: “We’re going to win, in the end.” But because of the climate crisis, we don’t have that much time. You know, there’s a point where if it gets too hot. Then there’s no going back.
	

	This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.



	

									Stafano Trovati|SGPC/Courtesy DvF

schema.headline: Jane Fonda on Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger, Trump and Tech Bros’ Desire for Longevity ‘While They’re Killing the Rest of Us’

title: Dolly Parton Tributes Score Big Ratings for the Networks; ABC’s ‘9 to 5’ Airing Is Most-Watched Broadcast Movie in More Than Three Years
description: Dolly Parton continues to be a beloved icon — if ratings for the recent tribute specials across four different networks are any indication. ABC, CBS
body:
Dolly Parton continues to be a beloved icon — if ratings for the recent tribute specials across four different networks are any indication. ABC, CBS, NBC and The CW all attracted decent-sized crowds for quickly-scheduled specials that aired in late August — not particularly a time for major viewership.

	Among the highlights, ABC aired a repeat of the 1980 film “9 to 5” (a rarity in itself, for a broadcast network to run a movie that old) on Sunday, Aug. 30 that averaged 4.275 million viewers in live+same day ratings — the most-watched film on a broadcast network in more than three and a half years (since December 2022). It was also the most-watched film on ABC in nearly six years, since Dec. 20, 2020 (another classic, “The Sound of Music”).
	

	Parton died of cancer on Aug. 25 at age 80. That same day, ABC aired the ABC News-produced “Dolly Parton: An American Original — Special Edition of 20/20,” hosted by “World News Tonight” anchor David Muir, which averaged 4.051 million total viewers in L+SD. That made it No. 1 in its 10 p.m. time slot (beating CBS’ Parton special in that same slot) and was the best non-sports telecast at 10 p.m. in three months (since May, with NBC’s “Chicago P.D.” season finale).


	That initial “Dolly Parton: An American Original” airing has since grown to 6.556 million in multiplatform viewing via ABC, Disney+, Hulu and other digital platforms. On Disney+ and Hulu, “Dolly Parton: An American Original” was the most-viewed title on Aug. 26, during its first day of streaming.

	Meanwhile, also that evening, CBS News was behind “A CBS News Special: Dolly Parton—An American Idol,” anchored by “CBS Mornings’” Gayle King and “CBS Evening News’” Tony Dokoupil, along with CBS News senior culture and senior national correspondent Anthony Mason. The special averaged 2.085 million viewers.
	

	On Wednesday, Aug. 26, NBC aired “Dolly: An NBC News Special,” anchored by Lester Holt. The special initially did 3.952 million viewers, and has since grown to 4.5 million viewers with Peacock included.

	Also on Wednesday, The CW aired an encore presentation of its special “Dolly Parton: Here I Am,” which averaged 1.299 million viewers — a large number for the netlet.

	Then, on Sunday, besides “9 to 5,” ABC rebroadcast “Dolly Parton: An American Original,” which attracted an additional 3.566 million viewers.

	And on CBS that evening, with an assist from its “60 Minutes” lead-in, the Eye’s “Entertainment Tonight” special “Remembering Dolly: A Rhinestone Life” averaged 5.326 million viewers. That special, hosted by “ET” anchors Kevin Frazier and Nischelle Turner, included Parton’s first interview with the entertainment newsmag in 1982, all the way up to her final chat with the show. The special also included interviews and tributes from Dionne Warwick, Melissa Etheridge, Diane Warren, Debbie Allen, Jennifer Nettles and others.

	The Parton news also had an impact on the evening news broadcasts: On August 25, the day of Parton’s death, “World News Tonight with David Muir” averaged 9.2 million viewers; for the week, “World News Tonight” garnered its largest weekly viewership in five months.

schema.headline: Dolly Parton Tributes Score Big Ratings for the Networks; ABC’s ‘9 to 5’ Airing Is Most-Watched Broadcast Movie in More Than Three Years

title: ‘Lego Harry Potter’ Collection Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 (Gaming News Roundup)
description:
The “Lego Harry Potter Collection” is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on Oct. 16.

	Developed by Warner Bros. Games, TT Games and The Lego Group, the co
body:
The “Lego Harry Potter Collection” is coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on Oct. 16.

	Developed by Warner Bros. Games, TT Games and The Lego Group, the collection includes “Lego Harry Potter: Years 1-4” and “Lego Harry Potter: Years 5-7.” The Nintendo Switch 2 version of the collection will be available in both physical and digital versions, with the physical edition including both games on one key card.


	The first four years of the game draw from the first four films — ” Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone,” “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” “Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban” and Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” — allowing fans to experience Harry’s first years at Hogwarts through Legos. “Lego Harry Potter: Years 5-7” transports players through the final four films — ” Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix,” “Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince” and “Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows” Part 1 & 2 — to experience Harry’s last years at Hogwarts and his ultimate showdown with Voldemort.
	

	Preorders are available now for this classic compilation, which brings together “Lego Harry Potter: Years 1-4″ and “Lego Harry Potter: Years 5-7,” as well as all previously released downloadable content packs in one magical package for $49.99.



	See more gaming news from the week below.
	
		RELEASE DATES	

	“Final Fantasy VII Revelation” will launch on April 8, 2027 across all modern platforms. Preorders are available now across PlayStation 5, PC, Xbox Series X|S and Nintendo Switch 2.
	

	Square Enix released a new trailer and gameplay footage of the finale of the franchise. Players can mount up with Piko, learn new traversal and combat abilities, master the hybrid combat system and see Cid and Vincent wearing the Knight and Summoner outfits in the extended gameplay deep dive. In the game, they will be able to swap their active, controlled character, as well as their party makeup, at any time while exploring the world. They can also quickly scale rooftops and nimbly zip through the environment with the new grappling gun.

	Physical and digital preorders are available now, with digital Nintendo Switch 2 preorders opening at a later date. Players can preorder the following editions at global retailers and the Square Enix Store. 

	Watch the “Final Fantasy VII Revelation” release date trailer below.


	
		NEW RELEASES 	

	“Orbitals” launched Thursday on Nintendo Switch 2 and the Nintendo Switch via the Nintendo eShop. 

	In the two-player co-op adventure, Maki and Omura brave the dangerous Storm Wall and otherworldly threats to save their home

	*

	“NBA 2K27” launches Friday across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S, PC via Steam, and Nintendo Switch 2.

	From developer Visual Concepts, this marks the latest iteration of the NBA video game franchise published by 2K.

	*

	“Onimusha: Way of the Sword” will launch Friday across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S and X, PC and Nintendo Switch 2. 

	The Capcom-developed title takes place in an action-filled dark fantasy Kyoto taken over by invaders. It’s up to samurai Miyamoto Musashi to drive the deadly Gemma back into the underworld. 

	*

	“Isle of Reveries” debuts Friday from indie developer Desertcucco. The game will be available on PC via Steam, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

	Per the Steam description for the game, “Make a pilgrimage skybound to the Isle of Reveries, where any wish can be granted. Conquer mysterious dungeons, solve puzzles, and explore a vast overworld in this retro-inspired adventure.”
	
	
		NEWLY ANNOUNCED GAMES	

	The New York Times is introducing a series of bonus puzzles released every Wednesday for Games and All Access subscribers starting Sept. 2. 

	These puzzles are The New York Times’s classic games with a twist, including “Wordle in 1,” “Connections 3×3,” “Colorful Strands,” “Mystery Mini,” “Easy Mode Crossword” and “Special Crossword.” 

	“Wordle in 1” is a variation of “Wordle” where players are given one clue and there is only one possible word solution. “Connections 3×3” is a take on “Connections” where there are three groups of three instead of four groups of four. “Colorful Strands” is “Strands” with editorially-designed boards. “Mystery Mini” has the same rules as “Mini,” but with a twist to the presentation of the grid or the clues. “Easy Mode Crossword” is version of the “Friday Crossword” with easier clues. “Special Crossword” is a themed version of the “Crossword,” published on the first day of each month. 

	“Bonus puzzles are an exciting addition to continue diversifying our portfolio, with each puzzle built on mechanics that our solvers already know and love, but with novelty to make them feel distinct from the daily puzzles,” said head of games Jonathan Knight. “Designed for flexible, low-pressure play, the weekly drop gives solvers more ways to play with no daily obligations. And this new offering builds upon the value of a New York Times Games subscription, introducing fresh and exclusive puzzles that leave solvers excited to return for more.”

	*

	The Grinch is back, but this time he’s saving Christmas, not stealing it. 

	Outright Games and Dr. Seuss Enterprise are celebrating the holidays this season with “The Grinch 2,” a new 3D platforming adventure launching Sept. 18.

	Players looking for festive fun can team up in local co-op as the Grinch and Max, combining their abilities to uncover hidden collectibles, solve environmental challenges, and gather ornaments to complete Who-ville’s ultimate Christmas tree. From the icy slopes of Mt. Crumpit and springy mushroom-filled Who Wood, to the waterfalls of the Grinch’s Cave and the snow-dusted streets of Who-ville, each environment offers different platforming challenges and festive secrets to uncover during the holiday season.
	

	“The Grinch 2” will launch on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC. 

	*

	The NFL’s newest video game is putting the controller on the sidelines.

	Nex and the NFL launched “NFL Flag Heroes,” a new motion-powered game that lets players use their bodies to throw, run and evade defenders. Available Thursday exclusively on Nex Playground, the game features all 32 NFL clubs and puts players in the role of quarterback and team captain.

schema.headline: ‘Lego Harry Potter’ Collection Coming to Nintendo Switch 2 (Gaming News Roundup)

title: John Malkovich Fights Back Tears During 13-Minute Venice Standing Ovation as ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Storms Into Oscar Race
description: In what will surely be one of the biggest standing ovations at Venice Film Festival this year, Martin McDonagh‘s “Wild Horse Nine” received a thunde
body:
In what will surely be one of the biggest standing ovations at Venice Film Festival this year, Martin McDonagh‘s “Wild Horse Nine” received a thunderous 13 minutes of applause at its world premiere on Thursday night and stormed into the Oscar race.

	John Malkovich got emotional and McDonagh looked touched as the cheering raged on, with Sam Rockwell‘s partner, “White Lotus” star Leslie Bibb, leading the charge with plenty of hoots and hollers. In fact, it was a “White Lotus” reunion as Bibb’s Season 3 co-star, Parker Posey — who also features in the film — teared up while she fanned herself and mouthed how hot it was in the theater. As the applause continued, McDonagh and Rockwell went into the crowd, shaking hands and signing autographs.
	

	Set in 1973, “Wild Horse Nine” follows two CIA officers (Malkovich and Rockwell) who are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island shortly before the Chilean military coup that overthrew socialist president Salvador Allende. Steve Buscemi, Tom Waits and Posey round out the ensemble.


	Before the screening, McDonagh was joined by his partner, Phoebe Waller-Bridge, and was swatting away mosquitoes as he posed for photos on the famed red carpet. They were giggling as they took in the hectic scene around them. Bibb stood off to the side with Buscemi and clapped for Rockwell, who was smiling and waving to fans.

	“Wild Horse Nine,” which will compete for the Golden Lion, marks McDonagh’s third consecutive feature to launch at Venice after 2017’s “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri” and 2022’s “The Banshees of Inisherin.” “Three Billboards” won Venice’s best screenplay prize before earning seven Oscar nominations and two wins, for Frances McDormand and Rockwell. Five years later, “The Banshees of Inisherin” brought McDonagh another screenplay prize on the Lido and earned Colin Farrell the Volpi Cup for best actor before going on to score nine Academy Award nominations.
	

	Already, Malkovich is drumming up Oscar buzz for his role in “Wild Horse Nine.” A scene-stealer in his decades-long Hollywood career — appearing in movies such as “Dangerous Liaisons,” “Being John Malkovich,” “In the Line of Fire” and “Empire of the Sun” — Malkovich has been nominated for two Academy Awards but never won.

	However, he’s not quite ready to prep his acceptance speech. “That is an incredibly kind,” Malkovich said of the awards chatter at an earlier press conference. “For me, it’s a very nice thing. But the nicest thing is the film getting attention. And the film has several terrific performers, and it’s beautifully written and directed. That’s what matters to me.”

schema.headline: John Malkovich Fights Back Tears During 13-Minute Venice Standing Ovation as ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Storms Into Oscar Race

title: Radu Jude’s ‘The Diary of a Chambermaid’ Secures U.S. Distribution With Film Movement (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Film Movement has acquired U.S. rights to Radu Jude’s “The Diary of a Chambermaid,” the Romanian filmmaker’s first French-language feature, followin
body:
Film Movement has acquired U.S. rights to Radu Jude’s “The Diary of a Chambermaid,” the Romanian filmmaker’s first French-language feature, following its world premiere in Cannes Directors’ Fortnight.

	The deal was announced by Film Movement president Michael Rosenberg and Kevin Chneiweiss of Paris-based SBS International. 

	Produced by Saïd Ben Saïd of SBS Productions, the film will next make its North American premiere at Toronto before heading to the New York Film Festival for its U.S. premiere.
	

	Film Movement plans a U.S. theatrical release followed by VOD, digital and home entertainment.


	“The Diary of a Chambermaid” marked Jude’s 12th feature in 11 years. The prolific Romanian filmmaker, whose recent credits include “Kontinental ’25” and “Do Not Expect Too Much from the End of the World,” competed for both the Golden Bear in Berlin and the Golden Leopard in Locarno in 2025.

	“The Diary of a Chambermaid” is an adaptation of Octave Mirbeau’s novel which was previously adapted for the screen by Jean Renoir, Luis Buñuel and Benoît Jacquot. 

	Ana Dumitrașcu stars as Gianina, a young Romanian woman working as a housekeeper and au pair for a wealthy Bordeaux couple, Pierre and Marguerite, played by Vincent Macaigne and Mélanie Thierry. While cleaning their home and caring for their young son, Gianina counts down the days until she can return to Romania for Christmas and reunite with her own daughter. At the same time, she rehearses for a local stage adaptation of Mirbeau’s novel — the production that inspired Jude’s film — while navigating the seemingly benevolent condescension of her employers. 
	

	“Radu Jude is one of the most vital and inventive voices in contemporary cinema, and ‘The Diary of a Chambermaid’ finds him at his most tender without losing an ounce of his bite,” Rosenberg said. “In recasting Mirbeau’s novel through the eyes of a Romanian migrant worker in contemporary France, Jude’s film is both a sharp piece of social observation and a deeply moving story about a mother’s love for her daughter. We’re thrilled to introduce audiences to his first French-language feature and Cannes debut.”

	The acquisition expands Film Movement’s recent slate, which also includes Orian Barki and Meriem Bennani’s animated drama “Bouchra,” a selection of TIFF and NYFF; Stillz’s Venice Orizzonti title “Barrio Triste”; Chie Hayakawa’s Cannes competition film “Renoir”; and Dominik Moll’s upcoming “Case 137.”

title: Suno Kills Controversial Mary J. Blige Ad Where She Seems to Endorse the AI Music Generator (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Legendary R&B singer Mary J. Blige was on the receiving end of a barrage of online abuse after the release late last month of a video advertisement
body:
Legendary R&B singer Mary J. Blige was on the receiving end of a barrage of online abuse after the release late last month of a video advertisement circulated by AI music generator Suno, in which she is seen seemingly collaborating and responding positively to an AI-generated song that sounds remarkably like her work.

	There was just one problem: She hadn’t approved the ad, and the deal with Suno was made by an individual who did not have the authority to do so.
	

	In a statement to Variety, a rep for Suno wrote: “Ms. Blige is an icon who we all deeply admire. Ever since she broke onto the scene with ‘What’s the 411,’ ‘No More Drama,’ ‘The Breakthrough,’ ‘Growing Pains,’ etc., she hasn’t stopped innovating. That’s why we wanted to work with her.


	“We entered into a business deal with someone who presented themselves as Ms. Blige’s official representative. As soon as we learned this was not the case, and that Ms. Blige was uncomfortable, we terminated the advertising campaign.” Contacted by Variety, a rep for Blige had no further comment. 


	In the 85-second clip featuring Blige — which has been widely circulated online but at the time of this article’s publication seems only to be officially posted on Suno’s Facebook page — the singer is seen in a studio talking with an unnamed producer as he builds a track apparently titled “Pretty Flowers” that is similar to Blige’s classic work from the ‘90s and ‘00s. She asks him to add strings and then a beat, and watches, seemingly impressed, as the track is built in seconds. She seems to say the process is “amazing” and “dope,” although the way the video is edited makes it unclear what exactly she is responding to.
	

	A shorter, heavily edited video — in which Blige’s comments appear to be taken even more out of context — is also making the rounds online, although it is unclear whether that one was created by Suno or was pieced together by a person not connected to either party.

	The controversy arrived at a tumultuous time for Suno, which has had a highly combative relationship with the music industry in recent years. Although it has struck licensing deals with two top music companies, Warner (which previously sued it) and recently BMG, it is in ongoing legal action with Universal and Sony over unauthorized use of their copyrighted material, and was sued earlier this week by Grammy-winning Americana singer Jason Isbell and others, who claim the company has allowed users to produce tracks based on musicians’ identities with its models without their consent. Last month a German court found that the company was violating U.S. and German copyright laws.

schema.headline: Suno Kills Controversial Mary J. Blige Ad Where She Seems to Endorse the AI Music Generator (EXCLUSIVE)

Enes Kanter Freedom

                          Takes Chicago Sky to Court
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 3, 2026
                            1:50 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Former NBA star Enes Kanter is taking Chicago Women’s Basketball and the City of Chicago to court -- demanding a permanent injunction lifting the ban on him, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            In his suit, Enes claimed that he believes deeply that the integrity of women-only sports must be protected and he had made public appearances on this point.
      
    
            He said he self-identified as a player who is eligible to play in the WNBA because, “such declaration is all that is required by WNBA’s rules and the related Collective Bargaining Agreement between the league and the players’ association.”
      

            Enes said his actions have led to him being the target of a torrent of hateful attacks and discriminatory actions based on his viewpoint and gender identity.
      
    
      
      Natasha Cloud scores, exchanges words with Enes Kanter, and he’s escorted from the game 👀pic.twitter.com/sHbIRLlrae
              @ClutchPoints
          
  
    
            Enes claims the defendants conspired together to execute their conspiracy to discriminate against him ... based on his verbal and his public behavior to express his viewpoint and gender identity when they wrongfully ejected Enes from a recent WNBA game on August 23 after he got into a verbal argument with Natasha Cloud.
      
    
            Following the game, he was banned from the venue after the incident and the team's owner called him a potential threat. Sources told TMZ, the WNBA did not plan to ban Enes from the league.

title: Musician, Pregnant Wife and 3-Year-Old Daughter Shot to Death in Mexico
description:
Mexican Musician
                          Executed With Pregnant Wife And 3-Year-Old Daughter ..
body:
Mexican Musician
                          Executed With Pregnant Wife And 3-Year-Old Daughter ...
                          6-Year-Old Boy Spared
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 3, 2026
                            6:39 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 3, 2026
                                2:34 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A rock musician was shot to death and found Tuesday in Mexico, along with most of his family, including his pregnant wife and 3-year-old daughter, according to CNN.
      
    
            The news outlet reported that Jonathan Meléndez, a 35-year-old keyboardist for indie rock band Camilo Séptimo, was gunned down with his wife, Ana Paula, 35, who was 4 months pregnant, inside their upscale home in Mexico City.
      
    
            Melendez's young daughter was also fatally shot along with her 21-year-old nanny, CNN said, citing the Mexico Attorney General’s Office.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Attorney General said 3 of the victims -- including the daughter -- were shot in the backs of their heads, while a fourth victim was shot in the back.
      
    
            The AG also said 2 victims had their hands tied, and the family dog was found dead with its legs bound. A 6-year-old boy was found unharmed at the scene.
      
    
            Police arrested two men in connection with the murders -- and prosecutors say one suspect used his relationship with one of the victims to enter the home.

title: Jax Taylor Reveals Alleged DM Ex Brittany Sent Over Fake Smartwater Deal: ‘This Looks Awful’
description:
Jax Taylor
                          Exposes Alleged DM Ex Brittany
                          Sen
body:
Jax Taylor
                          Exposes Alleged DM Ex Brittany
                          Sent Over His Fake Smartwater Deal
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 3, 2026
                            1:45 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Jax Taylor claims his estranged wife, Brittany Cartwright, has been trying to mess with his business deals for years … even claiming she reached out to Smartwater to try to cancel a deal that the company said didn't exist in the first place ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            TMZ obtained court docs filed by Jax as part of his effort to obtain a restraining order against Brittany. Jax said he received what he believed to be a legitimate invitation from a third-party influencer platform to sponsor Smartwater on his social media platforms and says he accepted the deal and posted some content about the company.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            He said he later learned the deal was a hoax but says Brittany clowned him on her podcast over the incident, even though Jax says he promptly removed his posts about Smartwater when he learned the offer wasn't legit.
      
    
            Before he deleted the posts, Jax claims Brittany reached out to Smartwater via DM, writing, “Hello. I just saw that you are partnering with Jax Taylor. Please know that this looks awful for your company, as he has a long history of abuse and disgusting behavior. This partnership does not reflect well on you."
      

            He says Smartwater responded to her, writing, “Thank you for reaching out. Smartwater has no relationship with Jax Taylor. He is not a brand ambassador, and his content is not authorized by or affiliated with the company.”
      
    
            He said he later learned Brittany spoke badly about him on her podcast with their former "Vanderpump Rules" costar Tom Schwartz. She told Tom that Jax “faked a brand partnership” so people would think companies were wanting to work with him.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            In his filing, Jax asked the court to stop Brittany from reaching out to his brand deals or business partners … claiming she also cost him his deal on the Fox reality show "Special Forces."
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Jax was granted a temporary restraining order days after Brittany got one granted against Jax.

title: Late NASCAR Star Greg Biffle’s Ex-Wife Seeking $10 Million from Estate Over Daughter’s Death in Plane Crash
description:
Late NASCAR Driver Greg Biffle
                          Ex-Wife Wants $10 Million From Estate
body:
Late NASCAR Driver Greg Biffle
                          Ex-Wife Wants $10 Million From Estate
                          After Daughter Dies In Tragic Plane Crash
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 3, 2026
                            12:58 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 3, 2026
                                1:43 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Late NASCAR star Greg Biffle’s ex-wife, Nicole Biffle, wants his estate to pay hefty damages after she lost her daughter in a plane crash ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs obtained by TMZ, Nicole filed a claim against the late driver's estate in the amount of $10 million for Emma Biffle’s death on December 18, 2025, in North Carolina.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Emma was on board the fatal flight with Greg, and Nicole has already filed a wrongful death action against the estate.  In the new docs, Nicole is asking for an order preventing the estate from making any further distributions to ensure there is money left over to pay her claim and similar ones filed by the estates of others who died in the crash.
      

            As TMZ previously reported, Greg’s estate is facing three separate wrongful death lawsuits. The first two suits were filed by Dennis Dutton and his son Jack, who were on board the plane. The lawsuits filed on their behalf are seeking a total of $30 million.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The plane crashed minutes after the jet took off from Statesville Regional Airport.
      
    
            Nicole claimed her daughter was sick on the day the jet took off and asked not to take the trip ... but claims Greg was "insistent that Emma accompany him." She claims Greg and others were negligent, which caused the crash.
      
    
            Now, the estate is facing $40 million in claims over the fatal crash.
